newsitem.title: ITALY: Omnitel says Stet has not yet paid up.
newsitem.headline: Omnitel says Stet has not yet paid up.

text.p: Omnitel managing director Silvio Scaglia said on Tuesday the mobile phone group had not yet received 60 billion lire due from state holding Stet as compensation for a licence fee to enter the cellphone market.
The 60 billion lire sum represents partial compensation for the 750 billion Omnitel paid to take part in the race for Italy's second mobile phone licence.

"Stet hasn't kept its word on the 60 billion," Scaglia told a news conference. "As an Italian, I think it's an extremely embarrassing situation with regard to our international partners. It is inexplicable that it still has not been paid," he said.

The centre-left government confirmed in January that Omnitel, Italy's second mobile phone group, would be compensated. Omnitel had complained to the European Commission about the fee it was forced to pay when it started up in 1995.
Information technology group Olivetti is the largest shareholder in the Omnitel consortium.
Italy's other mobile player, TIM, which is majority-owned by Stet, did not have to pay such a licence fee.
Scaglia said that Omnitel now had 40 percent of Italian mobile phone subscribers against TIM's 60 percent.
He said he was not worried by the prospect of a third operator entering the fray soon and forecast that by the year 2003, "one in two Italians will have a cellular phone".
